classification.difficultyReason: Infer the overlap from two set totals and their union, then interpret exclusive regions of a Venn diagram.

content.prompt:
Use an appropriate Venn diagram.

In a group of 40 students, 26 play tennis and 19 play soccer. Assuming that each of the 40 students plays at least one of soccer and tennis, find the probability that a student chosen at random from this group plays:

answer.worked:
Let $T$ represent tennis and $S$ represent soccer. Everyone belongs to $T\cup S$.

$$\begin{align*}n(T\cap S)&=n(T)+n(S)-n(T\cup S)\\n(T\cap S)&=26+19-40\\n(T\cap S)&=5\\P(T\cap S)&=\frac{5}{40}=\frac{1}{8}\end{align*}$$

The tennis-only and soccer-only regions are mutually exclusive.

$$\begin{align*}n(\text{only one sport})&=(26-5)+(19-5)\\n(\text{only one sport})&=35\\P(\text{only one sport})&=\frac{35}{40}=\frac{7}{8}\end{align*}$$
